content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The main contribution of the paper is to incorporate the point cloud of an object into a NeRF formulation. In particular, different MLPs are used to estimate different components required for rendering the scene. For example, there is an MLP for features, one for spatial, one for BRDF, one for radiance, and so on. Most of the components used in the paper are based other works.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: The proposed method obtains competitive results in lighting estimation and offers editing ability to deform an object.
Weaknesses: 
•	The paper proposes a system which is essentially based on NeRF with input using a point cloud.
•	The paper tries to demonstrate that the proposed approach can do many things and hence, there is a lack of focus. For example, from the title of the paper, it suggests that the method is focused on lighting and deformation. However, there are only two short sections on the experimental results. While the results on lighting estimation appear competitive, the results on deformation failed to demonstrate its advantages, in particular, with lighting. The shadows of the lego studs are not synthesized (see Fig. 4).
•	In Fig. 2, it is unclear why the results using the proposed method are good. For example, in the bottom row of the BlendedMVS, the results using the proposed method appear to be quite noisy and quite different from that of the GT while the results using VolSDF appear to be closest. In the paper, it says “… Table 1 and Fig. 2 demonstrate the effectiveness of SDF-based presentations of learning scene geometry.” This statement confuses me.
•	In the proposed method, there are quite a few hyperparameters, e.g. 3 in Eq. 11 and 2 in Eq. 12. There are no ablation studies to evaluate their significance.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: Without reviewing the Appendix, it would be difficult to fully understand the paper. The paper should be self-contained with the Appendix to supplement details rather than to serve as the source of the details. From this point of view, I would give a low mark to the clarity of the paper because it is unclear how the different parts fit together.
Quality: As stated on p. 2 of the paper, there are two goals of the paper: 1) to enable fine-grained geometry deformation and 2) to enable accurate illumination and relighting. Based on the results (Fig. 3 and 4), I am not convinced that the goals are achieved.  In Fig. 3, the recovered environment maps of the proposed method are quite different from that of the ground truths. In Fig. 4, there is very little, in any, relighting effects. For example, there is no shadow of the lego studs after deformation.  
Originality: The main contribution is to incorporate point cloud data. The other components are based on others' works.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper proposes augmenting NeRF using point cloud data to facilitate editing and lighting estimation and relighting. While the goal is novel and interesting, the results are not convincing that the proposed method has achieved the stated goals. In summary, the paper fails to convince me to accept the paper.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors aim to enable scene editing in neural scene representations. This paper proposes an SDF-based hybrid NeRF model that outputs point-cloud for better editability of geometry deformation in NeRFs and illumination and visibility estimation for relighting caused by scene editing. The authors adopt an HDR light probe image to represent the environment light and shadow mapping to approximate the light visibility after geometry edits. The authors compared their results with other implicit neural network methods in the tasks of view synthesis without editing, lighting estimation, and geometry editing.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
# Strength:
This paper is technically sound, easy to follow, and well-written.
# Weaknesses:
+ Technical contribution is not clear enough.
+ Quantitative evaluations are inadequate. Ablation study is missing.
+ The experimental results of environment light estimation and lighting update are not convincing.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Although the authors claimed that this is the first model that enables geometry deformation and "accurate" illumination and shadow updates, 
the previous work achieved each of the them. It is not clear enough what was the contributions to do them simultaneously.
They also did not evaluate the accuracy quantitatively, which should be in 7.3. Referring to Fig 4, the rendering quality of "Ours, w/. lighting" is significantly worse than the others. 

In the contributions, the authors include ***"new regularizations ... for mesh extraction."*** However, they did not explain the algorithm of the mesh extraction. Moreover, it seems to conflict with the statement ***"Closest to our approach are Yuan et al. (2022); Bao et al. (2022), where they achieve more flexible object deformations by using mesh-guided deformation. Different from their methods, we use point clouds as explicit representation, which enables users also use point-cloud for geometry editing."***
content.summary_of_the_review: Key points of the proposed method are not polished enough. More solid evaluations are needed to be accepted.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper:
The paper proposes a hybrid neural representation based on point cloud 
and implicit SDF to enable 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis of 
objects. It applies neural SDF to extract a high-quality mesh, and then register 
the point cloud to the mesh so as to achieve intuitive deformation of the neural 
scene representations by deforming the underlying mesh. It also learns the
reflectance properties of the scene so as to better model the shading changes after the 
deformation. The performance on novel view synthesis is comparable to
state-of-the-art methods. The paper also demonstrates results on geometry editing.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. The paper tries to tackle an important problem that previous methods ignore,
that is, predicting the shading changes after deformation. The paper proposes a 
systemic approach to handle this by learning a hybrid presentation with meshes 
and point clouds as well as scene reflectance.


Weakness:
1. It's not clear to me why it's necessary to incorporate the SDF in the
training framework. For me, the purpose of SDF is to get a high-quality mesh,
and it can be got with existing methods such as NeuS and VolSDF. After getting
the mesh, the point cloud can be registered to the mesh to enable deformation.
There is no need to also use point cloud to learn the neural SDF.

2. Similarly, when it comes to predicting radiance, two methods are used here.
One is predicting diffuse and specular radiance, and the other is predicting
reflectance and then rendering the radiance. If the goal is to account for 
shading changes after deformation, it seems that we can just use the second one.
The paper says "using the results from the specular radiance to supervise the
specular BRDF". It's not clear to me why such supervision is necessary, and 
the paper provides no ablation study on such a design.

3. The predicted radiance after deformation is not satisfying, and it introduces 
artifacts such as noise and blurriness (Figure 4). While I understand relighting
is a difficult problem, such a performance drop weakens the contribution of the
proposed method. Moreover, it's worth showing ground truth references when
showing results on geometry editing. Video results should also be included.

4. The predicted normal has high-frequency noise. What's the reason for the
noise?

5. The paper puts a lot of effort on comparing the view synthesis performance.
While I appreciate such efforts, it should not the main focus of the paper,
because the main components are from previous works, and it's not clear why
their combination would lead to better performance. Instead, it will be better
to focus on the editing part. If the authors want to claim the superiority 
of the proposed method in view synthesis and BRDF estimation,
more text and experiments should be put on what designs make it better and why.
What I agree with is that their combination enables you to achieve deformation and
account for shading changes.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. The clarity and quality is good. 
2. The novelty of the paper is not that significant, considering that it is 
a combination of previous methods such as point-nerf and VolSDF.  And there are previous methods that enable geometry editing of NeRF.  

3. The paper should be reproducible based on the information provided in the
   paper.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Overall, I have concerns over the novelty of the proposed method, and the
results in the paper, particularly for the shading changes after deformation, 
are not very satisfying. Therefore, I lean toward rejection.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a nerf-based method to edit the geometry and relight the scene. The key idea is to factorize the scene properties by inverse rendering, edit the SDF-based geometry and relight the deformed scene back to the lighting environment. I like the overall idea, and it is a challenging task for sure. The overall method sounds reasonable, but still leaves some unclear parts, as stated below. I hope to get feedback from the authors for a fair judgment.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength

The task is difficult, comparing to other nerf and inverse rendering work, this paper also enables geometry editing. 
The inverse rendering model sounds reasonable, considering both diffuse and specular parts, as well as shadows (not sure whether shadows are considered in inverse rendering, or only in rendering). 
The paper is informative. 

Weakness
I consider geometry editing as a main contribution here, but there are not much explanations about this part. I am curious about how exactly do you edit the geometry? You are editing the mesh or the nerf model? I think editing nerf is difficult, so if the editing is on mesh, then the rendering part is not volume rendering? It is surface rendering by the rendering equation? Is it so?

The illumination estimation is not accurate. I assume there is no gt for illumination, is it correct? The predicted illumination is very far from the actual lighting panorama as in Fig. 3 and Fig. 6 in supp. I also do not find any evaluation of lighting, as well as BRDF parameters, such as reflectance, specular reflectance and roughness. There are only table 1 consisting numeric comparisons, where Ours and Ours-BRDF (supposed to be the best?) are outperforming others. It is confusing me. Each part should be evaluated separately, not only the final results. There are no ablations either.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Good in clarity. 
Ok in quality and novelty. 
No codes provided.
content.summary_of_the_review: The problem is challenging and I do appreciate the overall design, but the performance, evaluations are insufficient. For now, I am on the fence, leaning to rejection.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
